description: Develop a Checkers (Draughts) game. Use an 8x8 board, alternate turns between two players, and apply standard capture and kinging rules. Prompt for moves in notation (e.g., from-to positions) and update the board state accordingly.

Develop a classic Sudoku puzzle game that uses a 9x9 grid. Each row, column, and 3x3 subgrid must contain the digits 1 through 9 exactly once. The program should allow the player to input values for specific cells, check for mistakes, and confirm when the puzzle is completed.

Implement a crossword puzzle. Provide a grid of squares with clues for across and down entries. The user can enter words by specifying the clue number and direction. The application validates if letters match and confirms completion when all correct words are filled in.
develop a program that detects palindromes in a given text file
Create a budget tracker to monitor expenses and savings
write a program that generates Fibonacci numbers up to a given number
Implement a two-player Tic-Tac-Toe on a 3x3 grid. Players alternate placing X or O, and the game checks for a win or draw after each move.
Implement classic Gomoku on a 15x15 board. Two players place stones, aiming to get five in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
Implement standard chess, fully playable in a Linux terminal with formal algebraic notation (e.g., Ke8). Enforce check and checkmate rules.
Create a standard 4x4 version of 2048. Slide tiles in four directions, merging equal tiles and tracking score until no moves remain.
Build a roguelike on an 80x80 grid. Use W/S/A/D to move, subtract monster HP from player HP in combat, restore 20–30 HP from treasure, and reach the door.

A standard New York Times style Wordle with a daily 5-letter word. The 5 letter word is randomly selected for each calendar day. Players have six tries with green, yellow, and gray feedback. Reveal the solution if not guessed after six tries.

Design a classic Minesweeper game with a 9x9 grid containing 10 hidden mines. The player uncovers cells by specifying row and column. Numbers on uncovered cells indicate how many mines are adjacent. If a mine is uncovered, the player loses. The game displays the board with updated markings after each move.

Develop a puzzle in which the user must group sixteen words into four categories of four words each, following the standard logic of the NYT Connections game. After each guess, indicate if the chosen words form a valid group. The game ends when the user forms all four correct groups or runs out of tries.

Implement a version of the NYT Strands puzzle. Provide a set of word segments that players connect to form valid words or phrases. Each connected segment should produce a meaningful solution. The user navigates by making selections and receives confirmation for correct strand formations.

Design a classic Snake game. The player controls a snake using directional inputs to move around the board and eat 'food' items. Each time the snake eats, it grows in length. The game ends if the snake collides with itself or the boundary. The board updates after each move.

Implement a standard Connect Four game. Two players alternate placing discs into a seven-column, six-row grid. The objective is to form a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line of four discs. Players choose columns by typing a number, and the board updates after each move until a win or draw.

Design a trivia quiz program that presents multiple-choice or short-answer questions on various topics. The user enters answers, and the game tracks the score. After answering all questions, the quiz displays the total correct answers.

Implement Dou Dizhu (Chinese Poker) game for three players, one of whom is the 'landlord.' Cards must be played in valid combinations (singles, pairs, straights, etc.). The objective is to be the first to run out of cards or prevent the landlord from doing so, following standard Dou Dizhu rules.

Create a Tetris game. Tetrominoes fall from the top, and the player can move or rotate them before they land. Completed lines are cleared, and scoring increases accordingly. The game ends when no more pieces can be placed. The board updates after each move or drop.

Develop a Reversi (Othello) board game. Two players alternate placing discs on an 8x8 grid, flipping the opponent’s discs that lie between the newly placed piece and existing pieces of the same color. The game ends when the board is full or no valid moves remain.

Design a word-segmentation puzzle named 'Strands.' Provide multiple strands of text that the player must combine to form meaningful words or phrases. The program verifies valid strand formations and confirms completion once all strands are correctly merged.

Create a simplified version of Monopoly Go! with basic board mechanics: rolling dice, moving around properties, buying them, collecting rent, and handling chance events. Track player money and property ownership. Display relevant game information and prompt each player for decisions.

Develop an interactive storytelling game. Present narrative segments and branching choices. Player decisions influence subsequent story events. Track variables such as relationships or items that alter possible endings. Provide users with different paths based on choices.

Implement a match-3 puzzle game reminiscent of Candy Crush. Represent the board and let users swap adjacent candies to form matches of three or more. Matches are cleared, new candies appear, and scoring is tracked. The board updates after each valid move.

Build a Flappy Bird clone. The player presses a key to 'flap' and keep the bird from falling. Randomly generated vertical gaps in 'pipes' appear. Each successful pass increases the score. The game ends if the bird collides with a pipe or the ground.

Program a simplified Space Invaders game. The player controls a ship at the bottom of the screen and can move horizontally and fire shots to destroy descending alien rows. The game ends if aliens reach the bottom or the player defeats all aliens.

Design a Gold Miner game. A claw moves back and forth, and the player times a grab to collect gold or other objects. Each object has a value and takes time to reel in. The level ends when time runs out or the minimum gold value is met. Display the position of the claw and objects, updating after each grab.

Develop a two-player Pong game. Each player controls a vertical paddle, moving up and down to bounce a ball back. The ball bounces between the two paddles and off the top and bottom edges. Players score a point when the opponent misses the ball.

Implement the classic Mastermind code-breaking game. The computer selects a hidden sequence of colors (or digits), and the player attempts to guess it within a set number of tries. After each guess, show feedback regarding correct color and correct position.
